problem: ContextBundle is a read-only projection but imports lifecycle state helpers and storage repository/scope types. This reverses the dependency direction and keeps context inside the core SCC even though context does not own lifecycle or persistence mutations.

options.name: Keep ContextBundle coupled to lifecycle and storage
options.correctness: Preserves current implementation but retains the 8-package SCC and prevents context from becoming a stable input compiler boundary.

options.name: Own read-only projections in context and use a structural transaction reader
options.correctness: Keeps lifecycle as the only state mutation authority while moving only deterministic read projections and a minimal duck-typed repository contract into the context boundary.
options.complexity: Seven governed paths including compatibility imports, architecture regression and responsibility record.
options.migration: Create canonical context projections, make lifecycle names import those implementations, replace storage type imports with local structural types, and run full verification.
options.rollback: Restore lifecycle/storage imports in ContextBundle and local projection definitions.
options.verification: Projection identity tests, ContextBundle tests, Architecture Gate, full Quick, lifecycle and Chromium.

options.name: Require every caller to inject projection functions
options.correctness: Would remove imports but spread orchestration wiring through many tests and callers without changing business value.
options.migration: Change every ContextBundleBuilder construction and graph dependency factory.

rejected_reasons.keep-cross-package-projection-imports: It retains the wrong dependency direction and blocks context from leaving the SCC.
rejected_reasons.inject-all-projection-callables: It would add wiring complexity and touch many callers for deterministic read-only behavior.

deletions: Delete context imports of agent_core.lifecycle and agent_core.storage; delete duplicate lifecycle implementations of the read-only projection functions while keeping their public names as compatibility imports.
unknowns: The remaining 7-package SCC remains open debt.
State/Loop persistence simplification and real-model certification remain separate future targets.
selected_responsibilities: agent_core.context owns deterministic read-only projections prepared for model context.
agent_core.lifecycle remains the sole owner of Goal, Blocker and Clarification mutation and transition rules.
storage remains the sole concrete transaction repository authority; context consumes only the list_drafts_for_scope structural read contract.
preserved_hard_invariants: ContextBundle output fields and ordering remain unchanged.
Goal, Blocker and Clarification write paths and state schemas remain unchanged.
modules, kernel, resources, ledger, rag and utils remain outside the main SCC.
The dependency debt baseline is not edited.
cutover_strategy: Record expected-red, create canonical context projections, convert lifecycle names to compatibility imports, replace only ContextBundle's storage type dependency with structural local types, then run complete product verification.
acceptance_claims: context imports no lifecycle or storage package and is absent from the main SCC.
Lifecycle compatibility symbols are the same function objects as context projections.
ContextBundle behavior and transaction scope values remain equivalent.
The current SCC member count is at most 7 and all product tests remain green.
